text: My first experience with teeth cleaning was unimpressive. The female dentist (I didn't get her name) was very rude. I simply asked if teeth cleaning would be very painful, and she said, "I already told you there would be some pain and sensitivity, and if you weren't ready, you should schedule another appointment." Doesn't the patient have the right to ask? I had already planned to have the cleaning done that day. In the end, that female dentist made me wait in line for another appointment (I don't know if she didn't want to do it or what), even though I didn't show any fear. I've had teeth extracted before and I always asked if it hurt. Do patients not have the right to ask questions at all? Ultimately, I was referred to Dr. Tang for the cleaning. Dr. Tang was lovely and spoke very well. The assistant was also nice. But the female dentist was definitely not okay. If I have the opportunity to go again, I will choose to go with Dr. Tang.

text: The orthodontist provides excellent service; they give good advice and communicate well with clients. However, the counter assistant has a poor attitude. If I can't make my first appointment on time (even after rescheduling), the assistant will show displeasure, sigh, and give me a condescending look. When the assistant first started, they were polite and provided good service, but lately, their tone has become impolite while their words are still polite. The worst part was when I once saw a dental assistant sitting downstairs with a group of people at the counter gossiping about other patients. After a year of using their services, I'm starting to feel unwilling to continue because of the assistant's behavior. If it weren't for the excellent service from all the doctors (especially the female doctor), I would have switched clinics already. The reason for this is the assistant's poor service over time. Many reviews I've seen agree that the doctors are excellent, but the counter assistant is terrible, as they are the first point of contact. I strongly suggest that the counter staff receive additional training in customer service.

text:
The service from the staff was terrible. They need complete retraining on behavior and customer service, as they lacked manners and professionalism.

I had booked an appointment at this branch, but due to an unforeseen event, I needed to reschedule. The page used an automated system (bot) to inform me that I could come at any time. After that, I didn't read further messages and therefore didn't see the message from the staff saying the schedule was full.

Instead of considering that the customer might not have read the message or called to confirm before the appointment, which is standard practice at other clinics, the staff let me waste my time traveling there only to inform me that they couldn't serve me and I needed to reschedule because the schedule was full. This was despite the fact that there were no other customers present at the time. Other customers who called to confirm their appointments also didn't answer, indicating the branch was quite empty.

Furthermore, when asked why I didn't call to inform them that the appointment couldn't be rescheduled close to the scheduled time, the response was blaming me. I had already replied via chat (just a chat reply), and the staff continued to argue with me, which is highly inappropriate for a customer service position.

This is in stark contrast to other clinics I've used before. I have never encountered service like this before. This place seems to not value its customers. I would recommend anyone considering this service to go to another clinic for a much better experience. If this place doesn't care about its customers, customers shouldn't waste their time and money on such substandard service. There are many other places that are cheaper and offer much better service.
